why: The top k regions are the first k after sorting descending, so each query is a prefix sum of the sorted array. Sort once, build prefix sums, and every query is a single lookup.
hints: Each query asks for the k largest values. What order makes 'the k largest' a prefix?
Sorted descending, the answer for k is the sum of the first k elements: a prefix sum.
Sort descending, build prefix[0..n], answer prefix[k] per query. O(n log n + q), instead of O(n) per query.
pitfalls: Ties do not matter: with [6,5,5], top 3 is 16.
Return answers in query order, not sorted order.
constraints:
• 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 1 <= q <= 10^5
  • 1 <= num_viewers[i] <= 10^9
  • 1 <= queries[i] <= n
  • Each success value is at most 10^14 and needs a 64-bit integer.
